title: HPAP
bodyHtml:
Human Pancreas Analysis Program (HPAP)

https://hpap.pmacs.upenn.edu/; https://hirnetwork.org/hpap-overview

The Human Pancreas Analysis Program (HPAP) performs, analyzes, and distributes deep molecular phenotyping of human pancreatic islets and immune cells to understand the pathogenesis of type 1 diabetes (T1D) and type 2 diabetes (T2D).

Data Types

Donor Information

Comprehensive human donor data, including demographics, clinical diagnosis, donor history (including medical history, history of diabetes length/type), current medications, body mass index, HLA typing, islet cell composition, and measurements of auto-antibodies, C-peptide, and HbA1C

Cellular Phenotyping

Cellular composition, Morphology and Viability, Oxygen Consumption

Microscopy Imaging

Histology (H&E), Calcium Imaging, Co-detection by imaging (CODEX), Imaging Mass Cytometry (IMC)

Flow Cytometry

Cytometry by time of flight (CyTOF), Flow Cytometry

Hormone Secretion Profiling

Islet Perifusion

Immunophenotyping (T1D)

Cell type mapping with differential gene expression and chromatin accessibility analysis in PLN and SPL; Generation of memory B cell and T cell clonal atlas across different tissues (SPL, PLN, MLN) and blood; Specificity analysis on circulating antibodies and selected TCRs and BCRs.

Omics

Bulk ATAC-seq, bulk RNA-seq, snATAC-seq, scRNA-seq, Multiome (snATAC + scRNA), BCR-seq, CITE-seq (RNA+antibody-derived tags), DNA Methylome, TCR-seq, TEA-seq (ATAC+RNA+antibody-derived tags), spatial transcriptomics

Workflows and Standards

Schematic workflows and protocols detailing islet procurement and all experimental methodologies

Interactive Analyses

Interactive tools to peruse ATAC-seq / RNA-seq, multiomics, scRNA-seq, and genotyping data

Data and Resources

Explore HPAP datasets through PANC-DB, PanKbase, or Pancreatlas.

Funding

HPAP is part of the Human Islet Research Network (HIRN) and nestled within the Human Pancreas Analysis Consortium (HPAC). The program is spearheaded by three institutions (University of Pennsylvania, Vanderbilt University, and University of Florida) and is supported by two complementary grants from the National Institute of Diabetes, Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK).

More About the Resource

The Human Pancreas Analysis Program (HPAP) conducts molecular phenotyping of the human endocrine pancreas and immune cells in order to understand the events precipitating beta cell loss and/or dysfunction in type 1 diabetes (T1D) and type 2 diabetes (T2D). Because of the large donor pool and multifaceted datasets collected, HPAP is able to study the trajectory of diabetes development in donor islets and immune cells.

HPAP has generated accessible multimodal datasets from ten cell types and nine tissues derived from > 180 human islet donors to-date. Data types are diverse and provide insights into the genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, epigenomics, and cellular and secretory phenotypes of T1D and T2D.
